## LLM Recipe

### 1.7 Reinforcement Learning &amp; Reasoning

#### [Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25597>)

Decision-focused reinforcement learning post-trains a language model using the cost of decisions induced by its predictions, without differentiating through the downstream optimizer. Synthetic optimization and offline inventory experiments show why minimizing prediction error can miss decision quality, while cheap-feedback variants expose the bias and variance tradeoffs behind faster early learning.

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Catch-up selection of an original Friday November 20 cs.LG announcement within the exact 72-hour lookback; retain the November 19 receipt date and actual November 20 successful catalog discovery. Read scientific main pp.1-12, theoretical Appendix A pp.16-24, empirical/protocol Appendix B pp.24-30 and prompts Appendix C pp.30-32. Directly inspected p.9 Table 1, p.11 Table 2 and p.28 Table 5. The framework predicts optimization parameters, solves for their induced decision and uses negative realized decision regret as the response reward; within-instance leave-one-out baselines cancel the common hindsight optimum. Reward correction uses one independent Bernoulli coin for the entire prediction batch and inverse-probability correction, with explicit policy/moment/decision-procedure conditions rather than a guaranteed speedup. Three-seed affine-predictor experiments cover shortest path, knapsack and quadratic allocation; a 96-item knapsack study compares exact, heuristic, warm-start and correction feedback under one-hour budgets. In offline H&amp;M-derived inventory planning, Qwen3.5-4B with rank-16 LoRA and non-thinking RLOO reduces mean regret on 1,251 test instances from SFT 234.01 to 172.72, versus XGBoost 183.22. Negative-SPO+ RLOO gives regret 222.11 despite slightly lower prediction MAE. The best 160.53 additionally uses target-conditioned teacher reasoning-trace SFT and thinking-enabled RL, so its 31.4% reduction is not attributed to RL alone. No matching author code/project was verified in the primary metadata/full text; cited libraries are not claimed as this implementation.

**Limitations:** Compute-efficiency experiments use affine Gaussian predictors on synthetic knapsacks, not measured LLM training speedups. At five minutes correction with p=0.5 improves regret, but after one hour its mean regret is worse than exact RLOO; more updates can entail similar or greater total exact-solver calls. The estimator and stationarity analysis concern specified response-level stochastic-gradient updates under regularity assumptions, not every clipped, normalized or Adam-based implementation. Inventory evidence is one constructed offline task with hand-set costs/order menus and a 4B model; repeated training-seed uncertainty is not reported for Table 2 and no production A/B is reported. The thinking variant changes initialization/data and inference as well as RL. Broader domain transfer and fully reproducible author code were not established. No experiment was independently reproduced.

### 1.10 Model Evaluation, Safety &amp; Interpretability

#### [PosteriorBench: Evaluating Behavior Posterior Sampling in Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25735>)

PosteriorBench evaluates whether methods that elicit rare language-model behaviors preserve the original model’s distribution of those behaviors, rather than merely increasing their frequency. Its reference samples and explicit cost accounting reveal a gap between cheap elicitation and faithful posterior sampling, giving safety researchers a controlled way to compare coverage, realism and efficiency.

The authors sample 50 million responses for each of 20 prompts from Qwen3.5-0.8B, label seven lexical/regex proxies, and select 21 prompt-behavior tasks spanning approximately 1e-5 to 1e-1 probability. Each task holds out 250 hits; evaluation uses 1,024 fresh sampler draws, a 10% native-hit threshold with fallback scores, forward KL capped at 50 nats and reverse KL. Three replicates are averaged within tasks, then tasks equally; error bars are standard errors across tasks. Training-free methods plateau near 100,000 counted construction inferences, while posterior-sample SFT catches up around one million; adapted prior training methods show no consistent efficiency advantage over SFT under this protocol. **Limitations:** The main benchmark uses one 0.8B model, 20 short English prompts, responses capped at 50 tokens and seven simple proxies; it does not certify deployment tail-risk coverage. Conditional hits are reference samples, while behavior probabilities and KLs are finite-sample estimates. Capping and threshold-triggered fallback affect rankings; error bars omit shared reference/probability-estimation uncertainty. Counted inferences approximate compute and omit external prompt-writer calls, so they are not total monetary or latency costs. Larger models have only two tasks each and training-free comparisons; two more complex behaviors use model judges and longer responses. Current protocol docs distinguish shipped BF16/SGLang reference log probabilities from recomputed FP32/Transformers values. The billion-row dataset was checked through metadata/card, not downloaded or independently validated.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.1 Agent Architecture &amp; Planning

#### [Pro² Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&amp;D](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25357>)

Pro² Agent organizes autonomous machine-learning research around a persistent record of bottlenecks, proposed remedies and evidence, updating that record through targeted experiments before refining code. Matched ablations support this workflow on 22 benchmark tasks, offering a practical design for making an agent’s research decisions inspectable beyond a history of code edits and scores. Published-system comparisons use different resources, and the full 75-task results have only one run per budget.

### 2.2 Tool Use &amp; Environment Interaction

#### [SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26069>)

SheetAlign grounds spreadsheet transformations in task-specific workbook observations and API references, trains generation and review policies separately with edit-progress feedback, and selects candidates by agreement between resulting workbooks. Its small-model study shows how targeted inspection and execution checks can improve spreadsheet editing, while the four-candidate version trades additional inference work for higher final accuracy.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.5 Kernels, Compilers &amp; Runtimes

#### [LightningMoBA: Dynamic Routing and KV-Centric Sparse-Attention Execution](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26268>)

LightningMoBA reorganizes sparse prefill around key/value-owned work units, splits high-fanout tasks and overlaps query gathers with GPU matrix work while replacing fixed block budgets with score-relative thresholds. On five checkpoints evaluated with RULER at tensor parallelism eight and batch size one, it reduces generation-loop time by 1.20–1.60× versus FlashMoBA at matched average Top-16 retention, offering a concrete design for turning sparsity into execution savings. Controlled comparisons attribute most Top-16 gains to the execution backend, while dynamic routing becomes more useful at larger budgets; quality still falls on every model at 64K context in the main Top-16 comparison.
